Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Pueblo CO
533 PM MDT Sun Sep 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing moisture within increasing southwest flow will bring 
  rain, heavy at times, to area along and west of the Continental 
  Divide through the day Monday.  

- Widespread precipitation spreads across all of south central and
  southeast Colorado Monday night through at least Thursday, with 
  periods of heavy rain and possible flooding.  

- Warmer and Drier weather for next weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM /THROUGH MONDAY/...
Issued at 248 PM MDT Sun Sep 27 2026

Current water vapor imagery and upper air analysis has modest southwest
flow aloft across the region, with upper level ridging building across 
eastern Colorado ahead of broad upper trough digging across the West 
Coast at this time. Water vapor imagery is also indicating Hurricane 
Polo spinning off the southern California Baja, with abundant subtropical 
moisture spreading across Old Mexico into the Desert Southwest and Southern
Rockies at this time. Temperatures have warmed into the mid 70s to mid 80s 
across the plains early this afternoon, with readings mainly 50s and 60s 
across the higher terrain, as high level clouds increase from west to east
this afternoon. 

Mid and high level clouds will continue to increase overnight, as models 
indicate PWATS increasing to 150 to 200 percent of normal through the 
day tomorrow. While we can't rule out an isolated thunderstorm across the 
Continental Divide through the late afternoon/early evening, we will see 
increasing coverage and intensity of showers along and west of the 
Continental Divide through the day Monday, with increasing uvv ahead of 
short wave energy ejecting out ahead of the advancing West Coast trough. 
This, along with increasing orographic southwest flow, will bring rounds 
of moderate to heavy rainfall to the eastern San Juan mountains, where a
Flood Watch remains in place from Monday morning through Wednesday morning.

Further east, scattered showers and thunderstorms spread east across the
higher terrain through the plains through the day Monday, with the 
increased available moisture bringing the threat of locally heavy rainfall
with the strongest storms. The scattered coverage of said storms precludes 
the issuance of expansion of flood watches at this time. However, if storms
do form or move across area burn scars, or areas across the plains that have
seen recent bouts of rain, flash flooding will be possible.

&&

.LONG TERM /MONDAY NIGHT THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Issued at 248 PM MDT Sun Sep 27 2026

While latest models continue to point to significant precipitation 
across Rockies through the middle of the week, the details on location 
of the heaviest precipitation continue to fluctuate, as models differ 
on the location of reminents of subtropical system Polo as it interacts 
with the broad West Coast trough translating across the southern Great 
Basin Monday night and Tuesday. At any rate, showers continue to spread
east across the plains Monday night through Tuesday morning, as 
precipitation picks up in intensity again across the Continental Divide
with increasing difluence aloft with a developing strong upper low across
the Desert Southwest. 

The latest EC solution remains the strongest and furthest north with said
upper low, which spreads widespread precipitation across south central 
and southeast Colorado Tuesday night through Wednesday night, as the system
tracks across Northern New Mexico into the Oklahoma Panhandle, with 
precipitation winding down from west to east through the day Thursday, as 
drier works into the region from the north. The latest Canadian solution
is the furthest south with the system and driest, though does bring the 
potential for heavy rainfall across the southern tier zones, while the 
GFS solution is now in between the other solutions, and is much wetter 
across southern Colorado than its previous solutions. 
 
The latest NBM and WPC guidance has leaned wetter across southern Colorado
and does have 1 to 3 inches of QPF across south central and southeast 
Colorado from Monday through Thursday, with greatest amounts across
the higher terrain and southeast plains along and south of the Highway
50 Corridor. With that said, and if the current forecast remains true,
later shifts will likely need to spread Flood Watches across much of 
southern Colorado through this period, however, would like to see better
model consistency before issuing more highlights at this time.  With the 
Pacific origin of this system, snow levels will remain rather high, 
generally aoa 12,000 feet through out the period, with the potential for
2 to 6 inches of snow across the highest peaks of the southern mountains.   
High temperatures to remain well below seasonal levels as well through
Thursday. 

By Friday and into the weekend, warm and drier air within more westerly flow 
works back into the region, as upper level ridging builds back across the 
Great Basin and into the Rockies. This leads to a slow warming and drying trend, 
as there will be enough residual moisture to support more isolated afternoon 
convection.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TAFS THROUGH 00Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 533 PM MDT Sun Sep 27 2026

KALS: Southwest winds lighten overnight, turning more southerly 
before picking back up again Monday morning. Cloud cover will 
increase, with cigs around high-MVFR setting in as rain showers 
spread across the region, lasting through the end of this forecast 
period.

KCOS and KPUB: Winds remain around 10 knots overnight, with 
consistent mid-level clouds. Monday morning, rain chances pick up at 
KCOS, with lower confidence near KPUB. After 18Z or so, gusty SE 
winds pick up at both terminals, gusting 20-25 knots, with rain 
showers spreading across the region after 20-22Z, though confidence 
in coverage is a bit lower at KPUB. Clouds will sink towards MVFR as 
rain moves across the region into Monday evening.

&&

.PUB WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Flood Watch from Monday morning through late Tuesday night for 
COZ067-068.

&&
